title: Key Management
subtitle: Generating, storing, rotating, and revoking keys

content.text: Key management is usually the weakest link. Even perfect encryption is useless if the key is exposed.

content.code:
import boto3

# AWS KMS: generate a data key
kms = boto3.client("kms", region_name="us-east-1")

# Generate a 256-bit data key
response = kms.generate_data_key(
    KeyId="arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789:key/your-key-id",
    KeySpec="AES_256"
)
plaintext_key = response["Plaintext"]   # encrypt data with this
encrypted_key = response["CiphertextBlob"]  # store this, NOT the plaintext key

# Later: decrypt the data key when you need to decrypt data
response = kms.decrypt(CiphertextBlob=encrypted_key)
recovered_key = response["Plaintext"]

content.definition: Regularly generating new keys and re-encrypting data. Limits exposure if a key is compromised.

content.text: Never store encryption keys alongside encrypted data. Use a HSM or cloud KMS like AWS KMS or HashiCorp Vault.

questions.question: Where should you store encryption keys in production?
options: In the same database as the encrypted data
In a HSM or dedicated KMS like AWS KMS
questions.explanation: Keys should be stored in a Hardware Security Module (HSM) or dedicated Key Management Service, never alongside the data they protect.

faq.a: Encrypting the data with a data key, then encrypting the data key with a master key (stored in KMS). The plaintext master key never leaves the KMS.
